gen-dafont-neuropol-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Futuristic and a bit digital, Neuropol keeps its letters tight, with a slim slot where the c opens. And Pilcrow Rounded replies with warm, generous curves that refuse to close, so the sharp heading and the soft sans feel like two different voices.
gen-dafont-neuropol-fs-quicksand: Quicksand reads soft and approachable, its bowls round like blown glass. Neuropol's closed, outline-style letters sit against that openness, and the difference in lowercase height makes the pairing look deliberate rather than matched by accident.
gen-dafont-neuropol-general-sans: General Sans reads clean and professional, with a smooth path around every bend and an x-height that fills the line. Its openness is the pair's best quality, since Neuropol's closed, futuristic outline letters look tighter and sharper beside it.
gen-dafont-neuropol-switzer: Switzer reads wiry and approachable, with c tips that never creep toward touching. Make Neuropol small and its slim, closed digital letters would lose the room they need, while the sans-serif body keeps its wide, open footing.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-fs-amulya: Pulled-apart, neon-tube lettering up top. Neuropolitical's single line thickness runs through the whole alphabet, and Amulya's sans-serif curves, with their generous gaps, make the strongest contrast to that uniform glow.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-fs-spline-sans: Spline Sans reads approachable and contemporary, leaving wide gaps between curve ends and stems, so each word feels easy to enter. Neuropolitical belongs big and short, where its pulled-apart, neon-tube letters get room.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-almendra: Neon-tube letters, spaced like they were pulled apart one by one. Almendra takes over below with a dignified, bookish serif and a deep midsection, so enlarge it a touch if the heading's glow starts to overpower it.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-quando: Quando reads bookish and traditional, with sparse, wide spacing and a big middle zone in every word, which gives text a slow, unhurried pace. Neuropolitical's neon-tube heading is its opposite, so bump the body up a little.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-sora: Precise and geometric, Sora turns every corner without any pressure swell, and its c and s stay widely parted. And Neuropolitical's neon-tube heading, a single glowing line thickness, is the sharpest difference, set against that clean sans.
gen-dafont-nordic-fs-plein: Plein is reliable and clean, with a clear channel leading in to every round shape. And Nordic's cramped, monoweight letters stay powerful and ancient beside it, so a long passage would feel open and steady against that tight heading.
